title: feat(platform-objects): User Preferences and Identity Links leave Setup's menu; the User page gains a Preferences tab
body:
Fixes #23803

Clause-②: no

## What this changes

Item 3 of the card: "User Preferences" and "Identity Links" leave Setup's menu, and each stays reachable from the user its rows belong to.

- `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/setup-nav.contributions.ts`: the `nav_accounts` (`sys_account`, view `all_links`) and `nav_user_preferences` (`sys_user_preference`, view `all_preferences`) entries are removed. A comment in their place records why, and where the rows are reached instead.
- `packages/platform-objects/src/pages/sys-user.page.ts`: `SysUserDetailPage` gains a last tab, "Preferences" (en / zh-CN / ja-JP / es-ES, like its siblings). It is a `record:related_list` over `sys_user_preference` on `user_id`, with the columns `key`, `created_at`, `updated_at` (the `all_preferences` view's columns minus `user_id`, which is the page's own record), sorted by `updated_at` descending like that view, 25 rows per page with the list's own paging. It authors no `add` and no `actions`. The existing "Linked Accounts" tab over `sys_account` is unchanged and serves "Identity links" (measured below), so no second tab is added.
- Translations: the two ids' labels leave `en.ts`, `zh-CN.ts`, `ja-JP.ts` and `es-ES.ts`, and their recorded digests leave the three `*.source-hashes.ts` tables (an orphan digest reds `source-hash.test.ts`). Both ids join `DEAD_SETUP_NAV_IDS` in `setup-nav-dead-key-tombstone.test.ts`, with their reason in its header.
- Tests: the new `setup-nav-per-user-stores.test.ts` pins (1) no Setup entry this package contributes targets either object, by `objectName` or by a URL; (2) the User page has one related list over each object, keyed on `user_id`, accepted by `RecordRelatedListProps`, and the page parses through `PageSchema`; (3) the Preferences list shows a subset of the `all_preferences` columns and authors no `add` or `actions`; (4) `unlink_account` is a `list_item` action. In `caller-scoped-first-list-view.test.ts`, the non-vacuity control drops `sys_user_preference`, because no nav entry names it now and the population is derived from nav; a new case holds pin (a) for that object by name, and goes red if an entry names it again. No pin was deleted.
- Changeset: `@objectstack/platform-objects` patch, worded for administrators.

### Outside the claim's declared file surface

The claim's file surface did not list these three files. Each held a citation this change made false, so they are in one separate commit (`8f20415f1`) that can be dropped on its own:

- `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/identity-auth.json`: item `identity-auth.linked-accounts-social` cited `setup-nav.contributions.ts#nav_accounts`. With the entry gone, `pnpm check:platform-checklist` exits 1 (`ABSENT SYMBOL`, measured at `2abfd4b4c`). That gate is not per-PR CI, by maintainer decision, but `platform-checklist-watchdog.yml` runs it on `main` daily and files an issue when it is red. The anchor now cites `sys-user.page.ts#SysUserDetailPage`; the item goes from revision 3 to 4 as provenance only, with no clause change. After the fix it exits 0 (735/745 anchors resolved, 10 on the named residual).
- `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-account.object.ts` and `sys-user-preference.object.ts`: comments only. They said a Setup entry names the object's unscoped view.

## The card's other items

- Item 1 (one audit entry) is carried by #23890.
- Item 2 (Packages and Installed Apps) waits on the maintainer's decision card #23892.
- Item 4 (39 entries) is checked by whichever of this PR, #23890 and the #23892 work lands last. This PR pins only its own part: no top-level Setup entry targets `sys_user_preference` or `sys_account`.

## Measured before the change (`origin/main` at `497518c3f`)

1. **Producer.** `nav_accounts` and `nav_user_preferences` were at `setup-nav.contributions.ts` lines 186 and 187, in `SETUP_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS`, group `group_advanced`. Every other `app: 'setup'` contributor (cloud-connection twice, mcp, plugin-approvals, plugin-audit, plugin-auth, plugin-security, plugin-sharing, plugin-webhooks, service-datasource, service-messaging) was grepped for `objectName:`, and none names either object.
2. **The User page.** `SysUserDetailPage` had "Linked Accounts" over `sys_account` (`relationshipField: 'user_id'`) and no tab over `sys_user_preference`. The new tab follows the Sessions and Linked Accounts shape.
3. **Every preference row belongs to a user.** `user_id` is `Field.lookup('sys_user', { required: true })`. The record validator refuses an insert without it, and refuses a PATCH that clears it (`required` and `required_cleared` in `record-validator.ts`). A user delete turns the default `set_null` on a required foreign key into `restrict` (`engine.ts`), so deleting a user cannot detach rows. The one producer, objectui's `packages/data-objectstack/src/userState.ts`, writes `user_id: userId` on every insert. Nothing in this repo writes the object server-side, and tenant-wide settings live on `sys_setting` (ADR-0007). No live database was read, so a row written below the engine (a raw driver write) is outside this reading.
4. **Row actions on the tab and on the old grid.** Read in objectui at the pin `daeb77fc84` (the files read are byte-identical at objectui `main` `63d00da`). The object grid gates New, row Edit and row Delete through `resolveAffordance` with `listNew`, `rowEdit` and `rowDelete`. The related list gates them through `relatedNew`, `relatedRowEdit` and `relatedRowDelete` (`packages/core/src/utils/affordanceGrants.ts`). Each pair reads the same CRUD bit (managed-object policy and effective API operations) and the same grant, so New, Edit and Delete get the same verdict on the tab as on the grid. The tab does not have the grid's Import, inline cell edit, bulk delete or `by_user` grouping view. Those stay on the object's own list. Its route is unchanged (the console resolves `/apps/setup/sys_user_preference` from all objects, not from the menu), and a preference record's breadcrumb opens it. `sys_account`'s one row action, `unlink_account`, has `locations: ['list_item', 'record_header']`, and the related-list host offers a child object's `list_item` actions on its rows.
5. **Pins naming the ids or objects.** `caller-scoped-first-list-view.test.ts` (control updated, pin (a) kept by name), `setup-nav-dead-key-tombstone.test.ts` (ledger extended) and `source-hash.test.ts` (orphan check, satisfied by removing the digests). `console-page-nav-entries.test.ts` names neither.

## Search

"From the search" now holds through the user, not directly. Measured in objectui at the same pin: the command palette (`CommandPalette.tsx`) and the full search page (`SearchResultsPage.tsx`) take their object list and their record-search scope from the active app's menu entries. So after this change, typing "preferences" in Setup's palette no longer offers the "User Preferences" list. `sys_user` stays in scope (`nav_users`, and `enable.searchable: true`), so searching for a user's name opens their page, where both tabs are. Neither object's rows were ever searchable: both declare `enable.searchable: false`. A direct palette hit for an object no menu names would be an objectui change, and none is made here.

## Acceptance notes

- `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/platform-core.json`, the Setup and Account nav-surfaces item: its walk step names "Identity Links / User Preferences" among the Setup destinations and records "45 Setup destinations". It is prose and no gate reads it, so a run after this lands will not find those two entries. Not edited here: it is outside the surface, and the count is item 4's. No carrier.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts` (the comment above the per-user UI-state map) and `audit-writers.test.ts` (a case comment) describe an admin editing a row "from Setup's User Preferences grid". The behaviour they describe is unchanged, because an admin's edit from the Preferences tab is the same write. Only the place name is out of date. Not edited, because `plugin-audit` is outside this claim. No carrier.
- `showViewAll` on `record:related_list` (spec `RecordRelatedListProps`, default `true`, described as 'Show "View All" link to see all related records') is not read by any objectui renderer. `RelatedList.tsx` renders its View all link only when a host passes `onViewAll`, and no host does (objectui pin `daeb77fc84`). The new tab sets `showViewAll: true` like its eight siblings on this page. That is the default, so it changes nothing. Reported to the seat as a finding.

## Verification, at head `a6f35a120` (after merging `origin/main`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/platform-objects test`: 72 files, 1116 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/platform-objects typecheck`: exit 0 (`tsc` twice, plus `check:test-typecheck` OK). The three edited or new test files are in the `tsconfig.test.json` program (counted with `--listFiles`).
- `pnpm check:i18n`: exit 0, all 10 packages' bundles in sync.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` (no paths): 65 commands derived for the 16 changed paths. All 65 were run and exited 0. `--ran` reconciliation: 65 derived, 65 run, 0 NOT MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
- `pnpm check:platform-checklist`, `check:authz-resolver`, `check:error-code-casing` and `check:filter-alias-parity` (rosters under `packages/`) each exit 0.
- Ablation, one leg per changed behaviour. Each mutation was landed with `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which proves the anchor hit and that the blob is restored to HEAD:
  - re-adding `nav_user_preferences` to the contributions turns 3 tests red (the new nav pin, the tombstone's declaring-side case, and the new caller-scoped case);
  - adding `value` to the Preferences columns turns the column-subset case red;
  - pointing the tab's list at another object turns 3 cases red.
  - After every leg, `git diff HEAD` is empty and the blob equals HEAD.
- CI's families are not re-run here: read them on this PR's checks.
